Once again I'm not sure if it's a true "bug" or more of an oversight. When you select a file for your avatar, there does not seem to be a limit for the file size. Also you can technically upload a file that isn't a photo either by changing the files extension to be .jpg or .png or by changing the file type option in the explorer window to all files and selecting any file of your choice. It will still send the data to voat and after getting all the data voat sees it isn't a photo and says it needs to be a .jpg or a png. Someone did this with a video about 90MB in size and after about 5 minutes of uploading it gives them a "Server Error: 404". Here is their post about it: http://preview.voat.co/v/whatever/592

The main concern here is not that people could take up storage space since voat doesn't seem to store the original file but rather make a thumbnail from it. The concern is that it could maybe be used as a way to affect voat's bandwidth performance and bandwidth cost if used on large scale. Being able to upload large file sizes shouldn't be allowed and should have a limit. Maybe even have a cool down for how quickly you can change it?
